text: Frederic Bartlett's experiments with the folk tale 'The War of the Ghosts' (1932) chiefly supported which model of memory?
choices: The constructive (reconstructive) model, on which memories are rebuilt from fragments plus schemas
The storehouse (archival) model, on which memories are stored and retrieved intact
The causal theory, on which memory requires an appropriate causal chain to the event
The thesis that semantic memory develops before episodic memory
explanation: Bartlett's subjects systematically distorted the unfamiliar tale toward their own cultural schemas ('effort after meaning'), supporting the constructive/reconstructive model over the storehouse model. The causal theory concerns what makes a state a memory at all rather than how it is retrieved, and Bartlett offered no developmental claim about semantic preceding episodic memory.
